title: Natural appetite based meal management hack
summary: A short diet tip: schedule calories around your natural appetite to stay at maintenance or in a deficit without hurting mood or focus. If, like him, you can sleep hungry but function poorly hungry, eat most calories early and have a light high-protein evening; if you can fast easily but can't sleep hungry, delay eating and save calories for a big evening meal. Know yourself and experiment.

claims.claim: Being hungry or calorie-depleted causes mood swings and poor focus for many people, which can be a real problem in high-stakes or safety-critical jobs.
How you spread calories through the day can prevent hunger-driven cheating, whether you count calories or eat by instinct like him.
He does not count calories; he eats by instinct and is currently at maintenance.
He sets aside claims that eating calories early is better for muscle gain and fat loss; his concern is the person's well-being.
People split into those who can sleep on an empty stomach and those who can't, and those who can function hungry and those who can't; he is foggy and inefficient when hungry but can sleep hungry.
If you can sleep hungry but not function hungry, eat most calories early in the day, then have something lighter and high in protein after training and go to bed.
His family had a saying that they often 'had sleep for dinner': going to bed hungry didn't matter because you don't feel hunger while asleep.
If you can fast easily but can't sleep hungry, fast after waking and start eating later; the later you start, the easier it is to save calories for a filling evening feast before bed.
Know who you are and experiment with your diet, because people react differently to the same approach.
